### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

none of the above

### Question

Hi there! This discussion is not related with any of the mini modules but for a little advice request. You know during plugin development there are several scenarios where we just add print statements to debug things out at a particular stage of plugin flow.

Sometimes messages are too long to fit in the screen height. So what did you do to handle that situation to move through those long messages, because you cannot do much to move around other than `u,d,j,k` to move around.

In some of the streams of **tjdevries** I found that he can open messages in a split with a `Messages` command which looks like custom made. I tried to ask same question on his neovim config but haven't got any response.

I though maybe you might also face this issue. If you have any advice to handle that please let me know or just **close this discussion**

BTW I recently start using mini.pick with mini.extras they are amazing thank you!

comment_data.body:
Hi! Thanks for kind words!

Up until Neovim 0.12 it was indeed mostly `:messages` and navigate through it. The `u,d,j,k` (and `G` + `g`) was enough for me. The thing is, checking out messages is not that frequent operation for me.

> You know during plugin development there are several scenarios where we just add print statements to debug things out at a particular stage of plugin flow.

Printing messages is not the best approach of doing this. A better way is to add some global `_G.log = {}` array and append to it the data you want to see during debugging (don't forget to `vim.deepcopy` if there are mutating tables).

As this is a frequent operation for me, I had custom helpers which not so long ago I added to 'mini.misc'. Those are [various `log_xxx()`](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-misc.html#minimisc.log_add) functions. Together with [`la` prefixed snippet](https://github.com/echasnovski/nvim/blob/16a8f5e1c43a6e78236ae55d41eae7f9e8a9c624/after/snippets/lua.json#L20) and [dedicated](https://github.com/echasnovski/nvim/blob/16a8f5e1c43a6e78236ae55d41eae7f9e8a9c624/plugin/20_keymaps.lua#L142) [mappings](https://github.com/echasnovski/nvim/blob/16a8f5e1c43a6e78236ae55d41eae7f9e8a9c624/plugin/20_keymaps.lua#L140), this feels pretty smooth right now.

To answer the `Messages` command question, it should be a more or less concise implementation. See `:h nvim_exec2()` to capture the output of any command (like `messages`). Later post processing and maybe opening in a separate buffer is left as a homework :)
